solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Teach, perhaps, putting vermin in pastry

indicators.note: putting one thing in another places it inside, as the following 'in' makes clear

parts.note: a pie is a pastry dish
a rat is classic vermin

explanation.surface: A cook's instructions for a gruesome pie with rodents baked inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Teach' looks like a verb but is Edward Teach, the pirate Blackbeard; 'perhaps' marks him as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Teach, known as Blackbeard, was a notorious sea robber, so he is an example of the answer.

clue.text: Childhood companion to act as husband

parts.note: to play is to act a part
a mate is a spouse or partner

explanation.surface: A childhood friend grown up and now acting as someone's husband.
explanation.definitionFit: A playmate is a friend a child plays with, hence a childhood companion.

clue.text: Terrorise appallingly noisy party animal

indicators.note: something done appallingly is done badly, leaving the letters in a mess

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A rowdy reveller frightening everyone around them.
explanation.definitionFit: A roisterer is someone who celebrates loudly and boisterously, a typical noisy partygoer.

clue.text: Sibling betting on the nose loses nothing

indicators.note: nothing is the zero-shaped letter, and losing it means taking it out

parts.note: a bet on the nose is a bet for a horse to win outright
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A brother or sister who gambles on horses but never loses.
explanation.walkthrough: Betting 'on the nose' is racing slang for backing a horse to win, not each way.
explanation.definitionFit: A twin is a brother or sister born at the same birth, so a particular kind of sibling.

clue.text: Vigorous Chelsea regularly imprisoned in upper room

indicators.note: being imprisoned means being shut inside something else

parts.note: an attic is a room at the top of a house

indicators.note: taking things regularly means at even intervals, here every second letter

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: Someone energetic called Chelsea locked away in the loft.
explanation.definitionFit: Athletic describes someone strong and active, so it is a synonym for vigorous.

clue.text: Bear witness to being irritable about condition

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: testy means short-tempered
if introduces a condition

explanation.surface: A witness in court grumpy about the terms imposed on them.
explanation.definitionFit: To testify is to give evidence under oath, the formal sense of bearing witness.

clue.text: Mick Jagger, say, has to wait around holding energy bills

indicators.note: going around and holding both describe one word enclosing others

parts.note: to linger is to wait about
E is the physics symbol for energy
bills are posters or advertisements

explanation.surface: A rock star kept waiting while his electricity bills pile up.
explanation.definitionFit: Mick Jagger fronts the Rolling Stones as their vocalist, an example of a band's main singer.

clue.text: About to get obnoxious person to turn over fierce animal

indicators.note: turning something over flips it, so the joined letters are read backwards

parts.note: re means about or concerning
git is British slang for an unpleasant person

explanation.surface: Someone trying to get a nasty character to roll over a wild beast.
explanation.walkthrough: Git is British slang for a contemptible person.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiger is a large striped wild cat, a classic example of a dangerous beast.

clue.text: Quieter vehicle fuelled by fruit I discarded

indicators.note: a vehicle fuelled by something has it put inside

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: discarding the letter named throws it away from the word

parts.note: a lime is a citrus fruit

explanation.surface: An eco car running on fruit juice that makes less noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Calmer means more tranquil and still, so it works as a comparative for less noisy.

clue.text: Flies religious groups

parts.note: pi is short for pious, religious
lots are groups or batches

explanation.surface: Insects swarming in congregations of believers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flies' looks like the insects but is a verb: steers an aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: To pilot a plane is to fly it, so the verb form matches flies.

clue.text: Active Liberal returns and draws one's talents

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for active

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: Lib is the short form of Liberal
one is the Roman numeral I
ties are drawn games

explanation.surface: A politician comes back and sketches his particular gifts.
explanation.walkthrough: The single letter for 'one' goes before the word for 'draws', read as 'one is draws'.
explanation.definitionFit: Abilities are skills or aptitudes, which is exactly what talents are.

clue.text: Merkel ignoring last messenger from God

indicators.note: ignoring the last letter means dropping the final one from the name

parts.note: Angela Merkel, former German chancellor

explanation.surface: The German chancellor disregarding the final message from on high.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek root of the word means messenger, and in scripture such beings carry divine messages.

clue.text: Satisfied one avoiding beef?

indicators.note: avoiding something means leaving it out of the word

parts.note: beef is a kind of meat
a means one

explanation.surface: A vegetarian content to steer clear of beef.
explanation.definitionFit: Demands that are met are fulfilled, so the past participle matches satisfied.

clue.text: Cooking appliance heiress I tore back to see unclothed

indicators.note: back tells us to read the remaining letters from right to left
unclothed means stripped of its covering, so the outer letters go and the inside stays

parts.note: the phrase with its first and last letters stripped

explanation.surface: A rich heiress ripping something apart to catch a glimpse of it naked.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotisserie is a revolving spit for roasting meat, a cooking device.

clue.text: Be wiser than to report on monarch's improving health

parts.note: K is king, the monarch
a patient who is improving is now better

explanation.surface: A court bulletin announcing the sovereign's recovery.
explanation.walkthrough: The report reads like a headline: 'King now better'. K for king is the chess abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To know better than to do something is to be sensible enough not to, so it means being wiser.

clue.text: Secret societies take some time to form crowds

indicators.note: to take something in is to hold it inside

parts.note: tongs are Chinese secret societies
HR is the abbreviation for hour

explanation.surface: Clandestine brotherhoods taking a while before gathering in numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: To throng is to gather in a large mass, so throngs means crowds together.

clue.text: American solvers back then surrounded joint which had no lager initially

indicators.note: surrounding means going round the outside of another word

parts.note: ye is the old form of you, the solvers

indicators.note: the first letter of lager is to be taken away from the word

parts.note: the ankle is a joint

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned bar scene: solvers in a pub that ran dry of beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back then' is not a reversal; it marks the archaic plural you.
explanation.definitionFit: Yankee is an informal name for a person from the United States.

clue.text: Cross setter, say, about to get pregnant

indicators.note: about means placed around, enclosing the other letters

parts.note: e.g. means for example, say
X is a cross
pectin makes jam set

explanation.surface: An angry crossword compiler on the point of finding out she is expecting a baby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross setter' seems to be a grumpy compiler, but the setter is the gelling agent in jam.
explanation.definitionFit: Expecting is a gentle euphemism for carrying a baby.

clue.text: Doctor over the river one who can keep control of Balls?

definitions.text: one who can keep control of Balls?

indicators.note: lying over something covers it, so one part wraps the other

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor
the Ribble is a river in Lancashire

explanation.surface: A doctor beside a river, with a hint of politician Ed Balls.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital B suggests Ed Balls the politician; the question mark flags the footballing reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A footballer who runs with the ball at their feet keeps it under close control.

clue.text: I make tea for sheep kept by bishops

indicators.note: something kept by others is held inside them

parts.note: B for bishop in chess plus RR for Right Reverend
a ewe is a female sheep

explanation.surface: A churchman's servant offering tea while the bishops tend their flock.
explanation.definitionFit: To brew tea is to make it, so the one who brews is a maker of tea.

clue.text: Very expensive seat of learning located in what's left of medieval castle?

indicators.note: something located in a place sits inside it

parts.note: a medieval castle often survives only as remains
the OU is the Open University

explanation.surface: A costly university campus set up inside an ancient castle.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ruinous costs so much it could bankrupt you.

clue.text: Almost drain a device to attract attention

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is cut

parts.note: to bleed a radiator is to drain it
per means a, as in so much a week

explanation.surface: Nearly emptying a gadget designed to catch someone's eye.
explanation.definitionFit: A bleeper is a pager that sounds to summon its wearer, used to alert someone.

clue.text: Hesitate to pursue the two in trouble

indicators.note: to pursue is to follow behind, so this part comes second

parts.note: both means the two
er is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Pausing before chasing a pair who are in a fix.
explanation.definitionFit: Bother is mild trouble or inconvenience, as in 'a spot of bother'.

clue.text: Park official called up engineers

parts.note: rang means telephoned

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters read from the bottom

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers

explanation.surface: A warden phoning for military engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: A ranger is a warden who looks after a national park or forest.

clue.text: Part of speech graduate brought back I had to shorten

indicators.note: brought back means returned the way it came, so read right to left

parts.note: a verb is a part of speech
BA is a Bachelor of Arts
taken as written
had a meal, ate

explanation.surface: A graduate returning a speech and asked to cut it down.
explanation.definitionFit: To abbreviate a word or text is to make it shorter.

clue.text: Defy leader of Bolshevik party

indicators.note: the leader is the one at the front, so only the first letter is used

parts.note: its first letter
a rave is a dance party

explanation.surface: Rebellion against the head of the Communist party.
explanation.definitionFit: To brave a danger is to face it boldly, in defiance of it.

clue.text: Young animal somewhat short of power

indicators.note: a little short means cut slightly, losing just the final letter

parts.note: a cube is a number raised to the third power

explanation.surface: A baby creature that lacks strength.
explanation.definitionFit: A cub is the young of a bear, lion, fox or similar mammal.

clue.text: Several disheartened ducks go outside in northern city

indicators.note: going outside means wrapping around the other letters
losing its heart means the whole middle of the word is removed

parts.note: a duck is a zero score in cricket, shaped like O
taken as written before its insides go

explanation.surface: A few downcast ducks waddling out into a Scandinavian city.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck in cricket is a score of nought.
explanation.definitionFit: Oslo is the capital of Norway, well up in northern Europe.

clue.text: Huge soldiers

wordplay.note: a GI is an American soldier and a soldier ant is a kind of ant

explanation.walkthrough: Both halves are soldiers: a GI, the US infantryman, and an ant, as in soldier ant.
explanation.definitionFit: Giant as an adjective means enormous in size.

clue.text: Quietly sick after bowling an excessive amount

indicators.note: after means coming later, so this part is placed second

parts.note: in cricket, bowling is delivered in overs
p is piano, quietly in music
ill means sick

explanation.surface: A cricketer feeling queasy after bowling too long a spell.
explanation.walkthrough: An over is a set of six balls bowled in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Overspill is what flows over when there is more than can be held, a surplus.

clue.text: Take a turn from surgery, troubled about when to get nutritious food for cattle

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shuffled letters go round another word
troubled means disturbed, so the remaining letters are thrown into disorder
taking something from a word means removing it, leaving the rest behind

parts.note: taken as written
a U-turn
as means when, as in 'as I arrived'

explanation.surface: A patient leaving the operating theatre, unsettled about mealtime for the herd.
explanation.definitionFit: Ryegrass is a pasture grass widely sown as feed for livestock.

clue.text: Roger, possibly by the grace of God, captured by man of action

indicators.note: being captured means being held inside by the captor

parts.note: a doer is someone who acts
DG is Dei gratia, by the grace of God, on British coins

explanation.surface: A man of action seizing someone named Roger, maybe through divine help.
explanation.walkthrough: Roger the Dodger is a British comic character from The Beano; DG appears on British coins.
explanation.definitionFit: Roger the Dodger is a famous evasive schoolboy, so he is one example of someone who dodges.
